correctness.rationale: The scalar b=(1−sqrt(1−4/beta))/2 solves beta b(1−b)=1; E_beta is the exact solution of F(beta[b+(1−b)E_beta−1/2])=b. For epsilon<E_beta, each low node input ≤b+(1−b)epsilon and each high node symmetric; strict vector-field inwardness on all box faces. Since logistic derivative increases on negative inputs, full T=F(beta(Wx−1/2)) contracts each box with rate beta F'(z)<1, proving unique interior fixed point, full-dimensional invariant attracting basin and local exponential ODE contraction. For eps>E_beta, explicit two-node W=[[1−eps,eps],[0,1]] drives x_1=b outward from low/high face, proving only canonical-box threshold sharpness. Near beta=4 Taylor yields coefficient 1/12 and beta→∞ gives 1/2. Independently verified 56 scalar inequalities for beta and leakage choices; finite tests are corroborative.

value.rationale: Natural heterogeneous sigmoid threshold networks have a genuine question of how much arbitrary interblock leakage preserves every combinatorial binary pattern without imposing equitable or regular blocks. Explicit dimension-independent robust basin certificates and sharp failure of their particular boxes are useful quantitative stability facts. No claim of maximal actual multistability threshold or global classification beyond these boxes.
